chall1.die.title: Section 1: Identify chall1
chall1.die.goal: Use DIE to identify the platform and architecture before looking at code.
chall1.die.open.title: Give chall1 to DIE
chall1.die.open.body: Drag chall1 into the DIE window, or use the ... button beside the file field. Wait briefly for the scan to finish.
chall1.die.result.title: DIE has finished reading chall1
chall1.die.result.body: ELF64 identifies a 64-bit ELF program, AMD64 is its processor architecture, EXEC means it is executable, and C/C++ is a compiler-language clue. Close DIE after reading these fields, then open IDA.
chall1.ida.title: Section 2: Load chall1 in IDA
chall1.ida.goal: Load chall1 as a new file and let IDA build links between functions, strings, and code.
chall1.ida.launch.title: Open IDA and clear the startup notice
chall1.ida.launch.body: Some IDA versions show an About window first. It only contains version information, so click OK. If it does not appear, continue normally.
chall1.ida.quick_start.title: Choose New on Quick start
chall1.ida.quick_start.body: New tells IDA to analyze a new program. If this page is disabled in your setup, use IDA's File menu instead.
chall1.ida.select.title: Select chall1 in the file picker
chall1.ida.select.body: The attachment is named chall1 and has no extension. Select that exact file and click Open.
chall1.ida.loader.title: Confirm how IDA will load chall1
chall1.ida.loader.body: ELF64 for x86-64 matches DIE's result, and metapc is IDA's internal processor name. Keep the defaults and click OK.
chall1.ida.ready.title: IDA has opened the chall1 analysis workspace
chall1.ida.ready.body: Functions appears on the left and IDA View shows disassembly. Names such as main, strncmp, and fgets mean the basic structure is ready. Start with readable text next.
chall1.ida.deviation.about: This is IDA's version information. Click OK to continue.
chall1.ida.deviation.about.body: This window only shows IDA version and license information; it does not change the analysis. Close it with OK, then continue to Quick start or the main IDA window.
chall1.ida.deviation.quick_start: This is IDA Quick start. Click New to analyze a new program file.
chall1.ida.deviation.quick_start.body: New starts analysis of a new program file. It opens the file picker; if Quick start is disabled in your IDA setup, open chall1 from the File menu instead.
chall1.ida.deviation.file_picker: Select chall1 in this file picker and click Open.
chall1.ida.deviation.file_picker.body: The challenge attachment is named chall1 and has no extension. Select it and click Open. If it is not in the current folder, return to the course page and confirm that the attachment is activated.
chall1.ida.deviation.load_file: IDA has recognized an x86-64 ELF file. Keep the defaults and click OK.
chall1.ida.deviation.load_file.body: ELF64 for x86-64 and metapc agree with the earlier DIE result. Keep the default options and click OK so IDA can build function and string analysis.
chall1.static.title: Section 3: Follow a string to pseudocode
chall1.static.goal: Use readable text to locate code, follow its cross-reference, and convert disassembly into pseudocode.
chall1.static.open_strings.title: Open the program's string list
chall1.static.open_strings.body: Choose View -> Open subviews -> Strings, or press Shift+F12. Strings are landmarks that help locate code; they are not conclusions by themselves.
chall1.static.strings.title: Strings is open: find the input prompt
chall1.static.strings.body: Find Input flag:. It is the prompt shown when the program asks for input. Double-click it to jump to the string definition.
chall1.static.definition.title: You are at the Input flag: definition
chall1.static.definition.body: IDA named this text format. DATA XREF: main+7F says code inside main uses it. Click format and press X to view cross-references.
chall1.static.xrefs.title: The cross-reference list shows where format is used
chall1.static.xrefs.body: Select main+7F and click OK to jump to the code that displays Input flag:.
chall1.static.deviation.xrefs: This is the cross-reference window for format. Select main+7F and click OK to continue to the code that uses the input prompt.
chall1.static.disassembly.title: You are now in the part of main that uses the prompt
chall1.static.disassembly.body: The code passes format to printf, reads input with fgets, and later compares it with strncmp. Place the cursor inside main and press F5 for pseudocode.
chall1.static.pseudocode.title: Pseudocode presents main in a C-like form
chall1.static.pseudocode.body: Read from top to bottom: strcpy prepares the comparison target, printf shows the prompt, fgets reads input, strcspn removes the newline, and strncmp compares values. Copy the complete string beginning with moectf{ and ending with }, then submit it on the MoeCTF platform.
